members.name: Zoe Adams
members.backstory: Zoe was a foreign correspondent who learned three languages badly and one well. She has interviewed warlords and mayors and are unimpressed by both. Studies. Of what, she won't say.

members.name: Yuki Mori
members.backstory: Yuki ran the reference desk at a branch library. She knows where every kind of knowledge lives. Now the library is gone and she is the reference desk. Cataloging the Codex. Dewey Decimal for the apocalypse.

members.name: Ines Duarte
members.backstory: Ines is here. Her parents came from Casablanca; she grew up hearing Arabic at home, and still understand more than she can say. Grows flowers nobody can eat. Morale is a crop too.

members.name: Elena Petrova
members.backstory: Elena baked for a bakery that milled its own flour, dawn to dusk. She knows dough by touch — when it is alive and when it needs to rest. Her parents came from Manchester; she grew up hearing English at home. No relation to Nina. The bread argument is ongoing.

members.name: Mateo Alvarez
members.backstory: Mateo is here. His grandparents came from Toronto; he grew up hearing English at home. Gives the best haircuts in the village. Everyone's hair is longer now, so it matters.

members.name: Boris Kowalski
members.backstory: Boris was a blacksmith — real forge, real anvil, weekends at the Renaissance fair and weekdays fixing plows. He has the forearms of a statue and the patience of a river. His parents came from Novosibirsk; he grew up hearing Russian at home, and still understand more than he can say. Forges tools from scrap. The ring of the anvil is the village clock.

beats.text: A man, maybe 40s has been asking about the strange leaves all week — "but what IS it?" Tonight, an answer. Ines drew big heart-shaped leaves on stalks, like elephant ears in the dirt for the others. It'll wash away. The knowledge won't.

Booker spends the afternoon with the giant rhubarb-like leaves, round burrs, first-year = leaf rosette with no stalk — look, smell, the smallest taste, then waiting. An hour passes. Then another. Nothing. The fire nods. That's dinner, maybe.
💡 The giant rhubarb-like leaves, round burrs, first-year = leaf rosette with no stalk — THAT's what Booker was describing. Burdock. It clicks like a key turning.
📢 SYSTEM CHALLENGE: "Catch something! Anything! We want to see how you do it!" (Hunt an animal today for a reward.)
"Triage tents and broth for the sick, or half rations till it passes, or the healthy hunt hard to keep everyone fed. Pick — everything costs."
(Relief is open — triage, rations, hunt, or rally, from the beats row. Each option works once; the moment passes in ~3 days.)

🔥 The fire settles. Ines has been quiet all evening, and now everyone knows why. "Night Court — I put it down today." "No sound. That is the warning. The moon-shadow on the ground is growing — and there is no sound at all. Owls don't make sound when they hunt." "It missed — and it is already turning. The second dive re-aims at where you moved."
